recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. If the Security WG wants additional AuditEvent narrative guidance or regenerated diagram tooltips, handle that as a separate source/generation decision; FHIR-53882's accepted element-definition clarification is already present.
issue_request: FHIR-53882 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core AuditEvent. It asked for clearer guidance distinguishing AuditEvent.agent.type from AuditEvent.agent.role, especially around ISO 21298 functional and structural roles and whether security roles are a subtype of structural roles. The accepted resolution clarified that agent.type is how the agent participated in the recorded activity and need not correlate to ISO 21298 Functional Role, while agent.role records roles authorizing participation and may indicate ISO 21298 Functional Role and/or Structural Role concepts.
initial_application: Commit 21041c1f5b03e6d5abd1e72e9c385be3be440272, merged by HL7/fhir#4066 in deab26af0c61935e2d6038b30431df61bbb3dfcd, changed source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml from the older ISO-centric functional/structural wording to the accepted participation and authorization wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists auditevent=AuditEvent, so the AuditEvent StructureDefinition source is in current build scope. A January-February 2026 Zulip thread shows the same pre-resolution confusion about agent.type versus agent.role and John Moehrke's guidance that agent.role is broad while agent.type is participation; it does not conflict with the Jira resolution. Older wording remains only in generated-looking SVG tooltips and historical XML comments in mapping-exception metadata.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative AuditEvent StructureDefinition source already implements the applied Jira resolution, and the remaining older SVG tooltip was not edited because the workflow avoids source-changing commits whose only edit would be a generated-looking resource diagram.
